transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
The Supreme Court began a new term today with a significant case on climate change.
Also on the docket, religious rights, the Second Amendment and immigration.
NPR's Nina Totenberg has more on the court's agenda.
The number of emergency appeals during the Trump administration has ballooned, while
the number of fully briefed and argued cases has plummeted.
And the result of all that is that the Trump administration has managed, at least in the
short run, to block most of the lower court decisions it doesn't like.
That said, of course, the court will be hearing lots of fully briefed and argued cases.
In addition, big test cases on immigration, guns, religion, climate change, and of course
the upcoming election is likely to make at least a guest appearance.
NPR's Nina Totenberg reporting.
Vice President J.D. Vance is heading to Alaska today to speak at a rally to boost support
for his Republican colleagues in the upcoming midterm elections.
It's part of a broader campaign push, with President Trump also planning to visit Alaska
later this month.
Alaska Public Media's Shelby Herbert has more.
The vice president is scheduled to speak inside a hangar at Fairbanks International Airport.
He'll accompany incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan, as well as his wife and children, according
to recent social media posts by Second Lady Usha Vance.
President Trump is also expected to visit Anchorage later this month to campaign for
Sullivan, who's facing Democrat Mary Peltola in a closely watched Senate race.
It's unclear whether those visits will boost Republicans' chances in November, though
Trump won Alaska by 13 percentage points in 2024.
Recent polling has showed the state's likely voters disapproving of Trump's job performance.
For NPR News, I'm Shelby Herbert in Fairbanks.
Minnesota's candidates for governor say they'll prioritize cancer prevention and treatment
as part of their health care policies.
Both are cancer survivors, as Minnesota Public Radio's Dana Ferguson reports.
Republican Lisa Daimath and Democrat Amy Klobuchar both experience breast cancer and
underwent treatment.
Both are now cancer-free and say they will prioritize cancer care access.
Daimath says rural care access is critical.
The opportunity that I've had to experience breast cancer and need medical care, I want
to make sure that's available for all Minnesotans.
Klobuchar wants to boost medical research in the state, add new tax credits to help
Minnesotans afford insurance, and fund early detection.
When you look at getting coverage for treatment and getting coverage for mammograms and all
of that, I understand how important it is.
Advocacy groups say either candidate could be an ally for cancer patients.
For NPR News, I'm Dana Ferguson in St. Paul.
Oil prices continued their sharp swings today, settling at a little more than $100 a barrel.
This is NPR News from Washington.
Ethiopia's Prime Minister says his country must have access to the Red Sea.
Neighboring countries say the sea's governance is for coastal states.
Ethiopia lost direct access in 1993, when Eritrea became independent.
Relations with regional neighbors have worsened recently, with renewed conflict in the Tigray
region.
Unpasteurized milk and other raw dairy foods are unsafe to eat and can cause serious illness.
The American Academy of Pediatrics warns.
NPR's Maria Godoy reports a new policy statement from the group says the risks are especially
high for young children and people who are pregnant or breastfeeding.
The updated guidance from the AAP calls for a ban on the sale and distribution of raw
milk and dairy products, including raw cheeses, because they can cause life-threatening infections.
While advocates of raw milk products say they offer health benefits, these claims are not
backed by scientific evidence.
Because dairy products can harbor pathogens like listeria, avian flu, and salmonella.
This year, an outbreak of E. coli linked to raw milk cheeses resulted in 13 illnesses,
including eight hospitalizations.
More than half of the people sickened were children under five years of age.
Three people developed severe kidney damage.
Maria Godoy, NPR News.
The remains of medieval ruler Tsar Samuel have arrived in Bulgaria after decades of negotiations
with Greece, Samuel fought the Byzantine Empire, and as a symbol of Bulgaria's national identity,
his remains were discovered 60 years ago.
The handover follows an agreement between the two countries to return religious relics.
I'm Rylan Barton.
This is NPR News from Washington.
This message comes from Lisa and their lineup of beautifully crafted mattresses tailored
to how you sleep.
Go to L-E-E-S-A dot com for up to 30 percent off mattresses plus get an extra $50 off with
promo code NPR.

Vice President J.D. Vance heads to Alaska to campaign for Senator Dan Sullivan in midterm elections
Minnesota governor candidates, both cancer survivors, prioritize cancer prevention and treatment in health care policies
Oil prices continue sharp swings, settling at slightly more than $100 per barrel
Ethiopia's Prime Minister says country must have access to Red Sea for trade and development
American Academy of Pediatrics warns unpasteurized milk and raw dairy products pose serious health risks
